key_insight: MedLatentDx lets hospital-specific AI agents share compact latent KV information instead of raw clinical text to support cross-hospital rare-disease diagnosis while better protecting privacy.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals diagnose rare diseases more accurately by combining distributed evidence across institutions without sending identifiable patient notes.
method: Private hospital agents keep local records and retrieved cases on-site.
They transmit compact latent KV blocks to a host agent for diagnosis.
Uses latent KV distillation for same-backbone setups and cross-family latent alignment for different LLM backbones.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on CrossRare-Bench, a large self-built rare-disease benchmark with hospital-level partitions, where it improved diagnostic performance versus raw-latent communication baselines.
watch_item: Latent representations may still leak clinical content, so real-world deployment needs careful privacy testing and governance.
paper_title: MedLatentDx: Latent Multi-Agent Communication for Cross-Hospital Rare-Disease Diagnosis
